title: Define Server Action ownership and throughput boundaries
businessContext: A team exposes internal action identifiers as its long-term external batch API and assumes unconstrained parallel dispatch.
problemStatement: Design the system for Human form submissions plus a machine client sending hundreds of operations/second. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Keep UI mutations secure and observable.
Provide an intentional external API contract.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: Human form submissions plus a machine client sending hundreds of operations/second
functional: Keep UI mutations secure and observable.
Provide an intentional external API contract.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Use Server Actions for supported UI mutation flows with input validation, current authorization and serializable state.

A client retries after navigation or a dropped response while the mutation committed. Stable operation identity, durable outcome lookup and receiver-side uniqueness prevent duplicate effects; action transport alone does not supply them.
alternativeApproaches: Yes, share explicit domain operations and DTOs while preserving each adapter’s authentication, request limits and transport semantics. Do not make the Server Component call its own HTTP adapter merely to reuse logic.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Test forged action inputs and current object permissions.
Load-test the documented batch API and UI actions separately.
Drop responses after commit and verify safe recovery without a second business effect.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
